extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, peer reviewers, and readers of randomised controlled trial reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting two-group, parallel randomised controlled trial manuscripts so that methods and findings are complete, clear, and transparent for publication and appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as a randomised trial in the title (Item 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification as a randomised trial in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should identify the report as a randomised trial in the title to aid indexing and readers; see related CONSORT guidance for abstracts. Appendix 1 notes simplified wording of item 1. Journals that endorse CONSORT should cite it in 'Instructions to authors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured summary in abstract (Item 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions (for specific guidance see CONSORT for abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a structured abstract describing design, methods, results and conclusions. Appendix 2: Item 1b — added sub-item on providing a structured summary and referenced the CONSORT for abstracts article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific background and rationale (Item 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific background and explanation of rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the scientific background and explain the rationale for the trial so readers can understand why it was done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific objectives or hypotheses (Item 2b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific objectives or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the specific objectives or hypotheses clearly. Appendix 2 notes Item 2b added a sub-item on specific objectives or hypotheses (formerly item 5 in CONSORT 2001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial design description (Item 3a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of trial design (such as parallel, factorial) including allocation ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the basic trial design (parallel, crossover, cluster, etc.) and allocation ratio so readers understand the study structure. Appendix 2: Item 3a — new item to clarify basic design and allocation ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important changes to methods after commencement (Item 3b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Important changes to methods after trial commencement (such as eligibility criteria), with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any important post‑commencement methodological changes and the reasons for them. Appendix 2: Item 3b — added to address changes to methods after trial start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for participants (Item 4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility criteria for participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear eligibility criteria so readers can judge applicability and potential selection bias. (Item 4 in CONSORT 2010 was formerly item 3 in CONSORT 2001.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Settings and locations of data collection (Item 4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settings and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the settings (e.g., hospitals, community clinics) and geographic locations of recruitment and data collection to inform generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions details (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe interventions in enough detail to allow replication. Appendix 2: Item 5 — encouraged greater specificity by stating descriptions should include 'sufficient details to allow replication'. For nonpharmacologic/herbal/pragmatic/cluster trials, consult CONSORT extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures (Item 6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completely defined pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary and secondary outcomes fully (what, how, when) so readers can judge measurement validity and selective reporting risk. Appendix 2: Item 6 — eliminated text on methods used to enhance measurement quality but added sub-item on changes to outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to trial outcomes after start (Item 6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to trial outcomes after the trial commenced, with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any changes to pre-specified outcomes post‑commencement and explain why, to reduce selective outcome reporting. Appendix 2: Item 6b — added because empirical evidence showed outcome switching occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size determination (Item 7a)
rubrics_metrics.description: How sample size was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the sample size calculation or rationale (including assumptions) so readers can assess power and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim analyses and stopping guidelines (Item 7b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, explanation of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim analyses or stopping rules were used, describe them and the rationale to allow assessment of potential bias from early stopping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence generation (Item 8a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the randomisation sequence generation method (e.g., computer random number generator) to allow assessment of unpredictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of randomisation and restrictions (Item 8b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of randomisation; details of any restriction (such as blocking and block size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the randomisation type and any restrictions (blocking, stratification) so readers can judge potential for allocation predictability or imbalance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation concealment mechanism (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence (such as sequentially numbered containers), describing any steps taken to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report specific mechanisms used to conceal allocation (not vague assurances). Appendix 2: Item 9 — reworded to emphasise reporting the actual steps taken to ensure concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who generated the random allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the roles of persons involved in sequence generation, enrolment, and assignment to detect potential sources of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking) — who and how (Item 11a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If done, who was blinded after assignment to interventions (for example, participants, care providers, those assessing outcomes) and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which parties were blinded and describe how blinding was achieved. Appendix 2: Item 11 — added specification of how blinding was done and, if relevant, description of similarity of interventions; removed requirement to report 'success' of blinding due to limited evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity of interventions (Item 11b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant, description of the similarity of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blinding depends on intervention similarity (e.g., placebo vs active), describe the similarity of interventions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods for primary and secondary outcomes (Item 12a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statistical methods for both primary and secondary outcome analyses. Appendix 2: Item 12a — added that methods should also be provided for secondary outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for additional analyses (Item 12b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for additional analyses, such as subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods for planned additional analyses (subgroup, adjusted), and distinguish pre‑specified from exploratory in results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow — numbers randomised/treated/analysed (Item 13a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, the numbers of participants who were randomly assigned, received intended treatment, and were analysed for the primary outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a participant flow diagram (strongly recommended) showing numbers randomised, received treatment, and analysed — this improves transparency about attrition and adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant losses and exclusions after randomisation (Item 13b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, losses and exclusions after randomisation, together with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report losses/exclusions with reasons to allow assessment of attrition bias and handling of missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment dates (Item 14a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give start and end dates for recruitment and follow-up to contextualise study conduct and potential temporal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why the trial ended or was stopped (Item 14b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why the trial ended or was stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reasons for early termination or stopping; Appendix 2: Sub-item 14b added based on empirical research about trials stopped early for benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics table (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present baseline characteristics in a table to allow easy comparison between groups. Appendix 2: Item 15 specified 'A table' to clarify presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers analysed and analysis groups (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, number of participants (denominator) included in each analysis and whether the analysis was by original assigned groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report denominators for analyses and state whether analyses were by original assigned groups (explicit instead of ambiguous 'intention to treat'). Appendix 2: Item 16 replaced 'intention to treat' with explicit information about retaining participants in original assigned groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and estimation (Item 17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each primary and secondary outcome, results for each group, and the estimated effect size and its precision (such as 95% confidence interval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results for each outcome with effect sizes and precision measures to allow clinical interpretation and meta-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary outcomes — absolute and relative effect sizes (Item 17b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For binary outcomes, presentation of both absolute and relative effect sizes is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both absolute and relative measures for binary outcomes for better interpretability. Appendix 2: Sub-item 17b added for clinical interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary analyses (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present ancillary analyses and clearly state which were pre‑specified versus exploratory to avoid over‑interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms and unintended effects (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: All important harms or unintended effects in each group (for specific guidance see CONSORT for harms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all important harms/unintended effects for each group; consult CONSORT harms extension for detailed guidance. Appendix 2: Item 19 included reference to CONSORT harms paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial limitations (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and, if relevant, multiplicity of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limitations candidly, including potential biases, imprecision, and multiple analyses. Appendix 2: Item 20 changed topic to emphasise reporting sources of potential bias and imprecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (external validity) (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalisability (external validity, applicability) of the trial findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on how findings apply to other settings, populations, or contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation balanced with benefits and harms (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure conclusions match results and balance benefit and harm considerations. Appendix 2: Item 22 changed from 'Overall evidence' to emphasise matching interpretations to results and balancing harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration (Item 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration number and name of trial registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide trial registry name and registration number; Appendix 2: Item 23 added because empirical evidence supports trial registration and journal policies foster compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol availability (Item 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the full trial protocol can be accessed, if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State where the trial protocol is available to allow assessment of adherence and selective reporting. Appendix 2: Item 24 added because protocol availability helps instigate adherence and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and role of funders (Item 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding and other support (such as supply of drugs), role of funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and funders' roles; Appendix 2: Item 25 added because evidence suggests funding source can be associated with estimated treatment effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow diagram (CONSORT Figure 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow diagram of the progress through the phases of a parallel randomised trial (enrolment, intervention allocation, follow-up, and data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A flow diagram is strongly recommended to illustrate enrolment, allocation, follow-up, and analysis phases — it improves transparency about participant flow and attrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and intent of CONSORT 2010
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT 2010 addresses reporting of what was done and what was found; it does not provide recommendations for designing, conducting, or analysing trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT to improve clarity, completeness, and transparency of reporting. It is not intended to be a tool for evaluating trial quality or to produce a 'quality score.' Authors, reviewers, and editors should use CONSORT in conjunction with the Explanation and Elaboration paper and relevant CONSORT extensions for specific trial designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CONSORT Explanation & Elaboration and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the CONSORT 2010 Explanation and Elaboration article and relevant CONSORT extensions for additional clarification and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explanation and Elaboration article explains inclusion of each checklist item, provides methodological background and published examples. Consult CONSORT extensions for cluster, non-inferiority, non-pharmacological, herbal, pragmatic trials, and harms guidance where relevant (see CONSORT website).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum criteria vs additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT 2010 addresses minimum fundamental items for reporting; authors may include other information if important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items included were deemed fundamental based on evidence; other desirable items (e.g., on-site monitoring) may be omitted if evidence or consensus lacking, but authors should not be deterred from including additional relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using CONSORT checklist to derive quality scores
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT is not intended as an instrument to evaluate trial quality or to construct a 'quality score.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist elicits clear statements of what authors did, but does not judge whether methods were appropriate; using it to create scores is inappropriate. Authors/editors should guard against fictitious reporting that complies with checklist wording but not actual conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to address checklist items somewhere in the article
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should address checklist items somewhere in the manuscript, with ample detail and lucidity; frequent subheadings in methods and results are helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT does not mandate a rigid article structure; adhere to journal style and field traditions but ensure each checklist item is covered (and indicate page numbers on a completed CONSORT checklist if requested by journals).
